![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/93489f5dd12c8dbbde799b4047965a89e4204f151c0b4dfc36286392775a05e2.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{4},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{4},$ where $\theta =m∠C.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{AC}$ adjacent to $∠C.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{AB}{AC} \\ \frac{3}{4} & =\frac{AB}{8} \\ AB & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 8 \\ AB & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot AB \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\cdot 6 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$
